title: Literature and references
text:
The terminology and methods used by weightedstate follow the literature on survival and multi-state analysis. Weighted Kaplan–Meier estimators are used in several settings, including inverse-probability weighting for causal inference. Keogh and Van Geloven (2024), for example, discuss weighted Kaplan–Meier curves after artificial censoring.

References
Aalen, O. O., & Johansen, S. (1978). An empirical transition matrix for non-homogeneous Markov chains based on censored observations. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 5(3), 141–150.
Keogh, R. H., & Van Geloven, N. (2024). Weighted Kaplan–Meier curves for summarizing the effect of a time-varying treatment on a time-to-event outcome. Statistics in Medicine, 43(1), 3–20.

text:
```{=html} # pragma: no cover



A package for weighted event prediction.



`weightedstate` implements a weighted Aalen–Johansen estimator for
time-to-event data. In the single-event setting, this estimator reduces to a
weighted Kaplan–Meier estimator.

The package provides one core function, `weighted_aalen_johansen`, for
single-event survival and competing-risk settings.

## Installation

```bash
pip install weightedstate

Single-event example

from weightedstate import weighted_aalen_johansen

times = pl.Series([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
reals = pl.Series([1, 0, 1, 1, 0])
weights = pl.Series([0.5, 1.5, 0.8, 1.2, 0.9])

weighted_aalen_johansen(times, reals, weights)

title: weighted_aalen_johansen()
text:
Calculate a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimate.


Usage
Source


weighted_aalen_johansen(times, reals, weights)


This function computes the probability of an event occurring over time, with support for weights. It can handle single events (like in Kaplan-Meier), or competing events (like in CIF).


Parameters


times: pl.Series

Event or censoring times.

reals: pl.Series

Event types: 0 for censoring, 1 for the event of interest, and 2 for the competing event.

weights: pl.Series

Non-negative observation weights.





Returns


 pl.DataFrame

Weighted risk-set counts, cause-specific hazard increments, overall survival, and cumulative incidence estimates at each observed time.

title: Estimation framework
text:
The Aalen–Johansen estimator is a non-parametric estimator of transition probabilities in a multi-state model. It is expressed as a product integral of cumulative hazard increments, estimated using a multi-state analogue of the Nelson–Aalen estimator.
In the weighted estimator, risk-set and event counts are replaced by sums of the corresponding observation weights. At each event time, these weighted counts determine the cause-specific hazard increments and therefore the estimated state occupation probabilities.

Kaplan–Meier as a special case
The Kaplan–Meier estimator is the two-state special case of the Aalen–Johansen estimator: an initial state and one absorbing event state. This relationship is preserved after weighting, so the weighted Kaplan–Meier estimator is the two-state special case of the weighted Aalen–Johansen estimator.
